name: Crimson Codex
description: Crimson Codex earns its name from the rust-hued mineral deposits that streak across its continental shelves, painting the landscape in shades of deep vermillion and burnt sienna. Towering mountain ranges rise like the spines of bound volumes along the equatorial belt, their peaks dusted with pale quartz that glitters under a warm amber sun. Vast rift valleys split the southern hemisphere, exposing layers of geological history in brilliant stratified bands.

The air carries a faint metallic sweetness, mingled with the rich loam scent of thriving fungal forests that carpet the lowlands. At dawn, the crystal caverns beneath the mountains catch the light and refract it upward through natural vents, casting prismatic halos across the morning sky. The fauna here—six-limbed grazers and canopy-dwelling gliders—move through the forests with an unhurried grace that suggests a world untouched by predation pressure.

Scattered across the northern continent lie the remains of a civilization that vanished long before any surveyor set foot on this world. Their structures are angular, carved from a dark stone not native to any known geological stratum, and inscribed with symbols that resist translation. A repeating signal, faint but persistent, emanates from somewhere deep beneath the largest ruin complex, cycling through frequencies no known species has ever used.

Xenoarchaeologists have petitioned for exclusive research access, but the planet's rich biomass and mineral deposits have drawn corporate interest as well. The signal's origin remains unlocated despite three expeditions, and the last team reported instruments behaving erratically near the deepest chambers. Whatever wrote itself into the stones of Crimson Codex left something still running beneath the surface, and the question of who—or what—will decode it first grows more urgent with each passing cycle.
